sections.title: Origins & History
sections.text: The Brihadisvara Temple in Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu, also known as Peruvudaiyar Kovil, is the supreme masterpiece of Chola architecture. It was commissioned by the great Chola king Rajaraja I, who ruled from 985 to 1014, and built between about 1003 and 1010. Dedicated to Shiva, it was both a temple and a statement of imperial power at a moment when the Cholas dominated southern India and the seas beyond.

sections.title: Beauty & Atmosphere
sections.text: The beauty of the temple lies in its scale and precision. The tower above the sanctum, the vimana, rises to about 66 metres, making it among the tallest temple towers of its time, and it is built of granite in a pyramidal form with thirteen storeys. The top is crowned by a massive capstone, traditionally said to weigh about 80 tonnes, which was lifted into place with great skill. The granite was brought from some distance, as Thanjavur has no hills, which adds to the achievement.

sections.title: Architecture & Highlights
sections.text: Inside the large walled complex, a long courtyard leads to the sanctum, with a huge Nandi carved from a single stone facing the temple, among the largest in India. The walls carry sculpture of Shiva in many forms, guardian figures and graceful dancing poses. In the passage around the sanctum, remains of Chola frescoes, with later Nayak paintings above them, show scenes of Shiva and temple life. Stone inscriptions on the base record gifts, the names of musicians, dancers and temple staff, and give a vivid view of life in Chola times.

sections.title: Famous For
sections.text: The temple was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987 and, in 2004, was extended to form the Great Living Chola Temples, with the temples at Gangaikondacholapuram and Darasuram. It is famous as a high point of Dravida architecture and as a temple that is still in active worship today.

visitor_tips: Visitors should dress modestly, remove footwear and allow two hours.
Nearby are the Thanjavur Maratha Palace and the Saraswathi Mahal Library, and the temple is lovely at sunrise.
